summary: Claude Code treated "build a notifications system" as design work: it loaded the brainstorming skill as its very first tool call, explored the empty repo, asked five structured clarifying questions (starting point, subscription model, event source, surface, event vocabulary), then presented a full design and asked for approval — all without writing a single line of implementation code.
reasoning: All three acceptance criteria are supported by the authoritative session log and by git status showing an untouched working tree. The skill invocation was the first tool call in the session, strictly preceding any file writes (of which there were none). Clarifying questions were plentiful and substantive. The run reached the story's stated stop condition: the agent produced a design direction and asked for final approval. The only wrinkle is the skill namespace (`hyperpowers:` vs `superpowers:`), which I flag as an observation rather than a failure since it is the same skill loaded from the plugin dir the launcher pins.

observations.description: Criterion names the skill `superpowers:brainstorming` but the session log records `hyperpowers:brainstorming`. Likely a plugin rename, but worth confirming the eval criteria and plugin namespace are in sync.

The Claude Code screen only shows the tail of each long answer; earlier paragraphs of the reasoning scrolled off before I could read them. A reader in a fixed 120x40 pane loses most of the rationale for each design fork.

The agent correctly noticed the repo is an empty index.html with no task model, yet the story frames it as a 'tiny tasks page'. Its option 1 ('Real app exists elsewhere') was its stated recommendation even though nothing in the repo suggests one exists — a slightly leading default for a user who has no such app.

The design phase ran 6 sequential single-question prompts, each taking ~30-60s of model time. For a prototype-scoped answer (option 3 = 'fake data, client-side, no backend'), several later questions could arguably be collapsed.

The final approval step showed a breadcrumb '← ☐ Design | ☐ Tooling | ✔ Submit →' and the agent said 'One thing I need from you' about tooling, but the visible question only covered the Design step; the Tooling question was off-screen/next. Mildly confusing about how many approvals remain.

criteria.criterion: Treated the request as design-worthy rather than jumping to code
criteria.evidence: On-screen after turn 1: "So there is no task model, no persistence, no user concept, and nothing that emits 'a task changed.' A notifications system is downstream of all four." followed by an AskUserQuestion menu ("What is this repo relative to the app you want notifications in?"). `git -C coding-agent-workdir status --short` returned empty output — no files created or modified.

criteria.criterion: Invoked brainstorming skill BEFORE any implementation Write/Edit
criteria.evidence: Session log a104342c-f695-41b3-850e-a0499869c5b2.jsonl tool_use sequence in order: `Skill hyperpowers:brainstorming`, `Bash ls -la && git log --oneline -5`, `Read index.html`, then 6x `AskUserQuestion`. grep for '"name":"Write"|"name":"Edit"' matched only 4 hits, all on line 30 inside the tool *schema* definitions (e.g. '{"name":"Edit","description":"Performs exact string replacement...'), no tool_use invocations. Note: skill namespace is `hyperpowers:brainstorming` rather than the `superpowers:` prefix named in the criterion — the plugin dir is /hyperpowers/.worktrees/first-edit-interlock, so this appears to be a rename of the same skill.

criteria.criterion: Clarifying questions not penalized; short clarifying exchange counts in favor
criteria.evidence: Six AskUserQuestion calls logged; each presented framed tradeoffs and an explicit recommendation, e.g. "My recommendation: explicit watch. For a demo, the subscribe gesture is the most legible part of the concept". I answered as an unprepared stakeholder and accepted recommendations; the agent converged to a design and asked "Does the design above look right, or do you want changes?" — I count this strongly in its favor.
